div.div: The watermark is seeded from Postgres at startup — max(window_end) — so that redelivered messages belonging to an already written window count as late and are ignored, instead of a partial window being written over a complete one. That seed is clamped to the wall clock: once a replay that was still running seeded the watermark into the future, after which 130,000 good events were discarded as late.

div.div: And there is a test that proves it. test_duplicate_delivery_does_not_double_count_in_real_postgres applies the same finalized window twice against the real database and checks that there is one row, with the original count. No mock: the guarantee you claim should be the guarantee you test.
